reason: E1 states phosphorus supports amorphization in HEMGs, and E2 shows P-containing CrMnFeCoNiP20 has a broad solidification range, supporting the first two premises. However, no cited evidence addresses the specific effects of a further 5 at% increase on liquidus temperature, cluster formation, or the quantitative improvements predicted, leaving the remaining premises unsupported.
premises: Phosphorus addition supports amorphization and promotes stable metallic glass structures in high-entropy alloys.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a broad solidification range and complex crystallization behavior due to phosphorus.
Increasing phosphorus content by ~5 at% will further lower liquidus temperature and broaden the solidification range.
The extra phosphorus will form stable clusters or phosphide-like short-range orders that suppress nucleation.
A 5 at% phosphorus increase will yield a 20–30% wider amorphization window and ~50 K higher crystallization onset.
